newsitem.title: CHINA: China '96 antimony output may hit 100,000 T.
newsitem.headline: China '96 antimony output may hit 100,000 T.

text.p: China's antimony output is likely to reach 90,000-100,000 tonnes this year if the government does not take steps to curb production, the official International Business Daily said on Wednesday.
China, the world's largest supplier of antimony, has seen domestic and international prices tumble in recent years due to excess production and smuggling to foreign markets, it said.

China produced 91,200 tonnes of the silvery-white chemical element used to harden alloys last year. Exports were 41,000 tonnes and annual domestic consumption stood at just 10,000 tonnes last year, the newspaper said.
Output was estimated at 40,000-50,000 tonnes in the first half this year.
China exported 21,762 tonnes of unwrought antimony in the first nine months, up 43.9 percent compared with the year-ago period, customs figures showed.
Rising production and stockpiles from last year's output would add more pressure to world price levels, it said.
The government must curb production and exports as well as put a stop to smuggling, the newspaper said.
China has already closed many small antimony plants in a bid to reduce output to stabilise world prices and cut pollution.
